newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
All papers
POLICE BATON CHARGE KASHMIR HINDUS

Police in Kashmir used tear gas and batons to disperse an angry rally of 25,000 Hindus protesting last week's killing of seven Hindus. Nearly 30 people including some policemen were injured during the demonstrations by Pandits, or Kashmiri Hindus, in Jammu city. The protests followed Friday's killing by unidentified gunmen of seven Kashmiri Hindus near Srinagar, the state's summer capital.
The Hindustan Times
MOSCOW TO GO AHEAD WITH NUCLEAR REACTORS' SUPPLY

Russia agreed to supply two nuclear reactors to India for the Kudamkulam power project. This put an end to speculation whether Russia would yield to United States' opposition to the supply of the reactors. At a summit meeting held between Russian president Boris Yeltsin and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in Moscow, Deve Gowda conveyed to Yeltsin that India had decided to go ahead with the nuclear deal and requested the Russians to prepare a detailed project report.
Indian Express
INDIA TO GET RUSSIAN MISSILES

Russia and India reached an agreement, in principle, on a proposed acquisition by India of six S-300V missile systems. A formal agreement on the deal would be signed soon, defence sources said. Regarding the supply of Ukrainian tanks to Pakistan, Yeltsin said he had stopped delivery of essential spare parts for the tanks manufactured by Russian factories.
The Economic Times
STATE BANK TO REVIEW PLR, MAY EASE DEBT-EQUITY RATIO

State Bank (SBI) will review its prime lending rate (PLR) after the Reserve Bank of India announces its credit policy for the slack season scheduled to be announced next month, SBI's chairman P.G. Kakodkar said.
LOUIS DREYFUS TO SET UP $8.75 MLN SUBSIDIARY

The Louis Dreyfus group proposes to set up an export oriented subsidiary in India for international trading and merchandising of agriculture-based commodities and value added food products. Sources said Louis Dreyfus proposed to invest $750,000 in the first year of its operations. In all, it planned to invest $8.75 million by the beginning of the fifth year. The investment to come through group's subsidiary Louis Dreyfus Asia, which would establish a wholly owned subsidiary in India.
RELIANCE, L&T READY FOR ROAD SECTOR ENTRY

Reliance Infrastructure and Larsen & Toubro are among the few corporates likely to approach the National Highway Authority (NHAI) to form joint ventures (JVs) to execute commercially viable road projects in the country. The government has decided to float seven JVs with private participation as special purpose vehicles in seven states.
Financial Express
AD-HOC T-BILL ERA WILL END WITH NEW PACT

An agreement between the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the government would put an end to a 40-year-old system of ad hoc treasury bills used by the government to raise funds from the central bank, and give way to ways and means advances. Sources said the ceiling on ways and means advances, which the government could take from the RBI in the next fiscal year beginning in April, was likely to be pegged at 100 billion rupees.
ENGINEERING GOODS EXPORTS LIKELY TO TOUCH $4 BLN

Engineering goods exports in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) are estimated to touch $4.04 billion, marginally short of the target of $4.33 billion. Exports during April-January went up by about nine percent to $3.04 billion over the corresponding period last year. In January, exports amounted to $354 million. It was estimated to cross $1.0 billion in the remaining two months.
RENEWED BOEING, AIRBUS BATTLE FOR AIR INDIA DEAL

Airbus Industrie and Boeing are involved in a renewed battle to clinch Air India's (AI) 25 billion rupee medium capacity long range aircraft deal. AI is likely to take up Boeing's claim of an additional 30 seats in its competing product, sources said. Airbus countered the claim saying there were no more than 12 additional seats per aircraft on an average as compared to its A-340.
STRICT NORMS FOR NEW RATING AGENCIES

The bourse regulator (SEBI) proposes to restrict the entry of firms in the credit rating business to entities experienced in credit evaluation. The draft of the regulations for credit rating agencies, which is nearing completion, also proposes to allow only institutional entities, including foreign institutions, to set up credit rating outfits.
Business Standard
OVER 450 ITEMS TO GO OFF RESTRICTED IMPORT LIST

The government plans to remove more than 450 items from the restricted list of imports and scrap the value based advance licensing scheme (Vabal) in the new export-import policy scheduled to be announced on March 31. The items removed would be put on the special import licence (SIL) and open general licence (OGL) list in the new policy. The passbook scheme and the negative list under the Vabal scheme would be scrapped and a simplified passbook scheme would be evolved. Duty-free entitlements for imports would be given against credits according to the sector/category.
VSNL GDR AT 25 PERCENT PREMIA

The global depositary receipts (GDRs) of Videsh Sanchar Nigam (VSNL) climbed more than $2.50 in international markets in the first few hours of their being listed at $13.93 on the London bourse. The pricing represented a 1.5 percent premium on VSNL's closing price of 985.25 rupees on the previous Friday. VSNL's $448 million GDR issue, the largest ever by an Indian company, included 3.9 million shares disinvested by the government and a 12.165 million shares in an initial public offering (IPO). VSNL closed at 1070 rupees on the Bombay bourse.
NORMS TIGHTENED FOR FOREIGN EQUITY HOLDING

The Finance Ministry has tightened norms for foreign investment in non-banking finance companies (NBFCs) by deciding on case-by-case approvals instead of automatic clearances. The minimum capitalisation for foreign equity of up to 51 percent will be $500,000, and for equity of 51 to 75 percent $5 million. For firms with a foreign equity of more than 75 percent it will be $50 million. For up to 75 percent, the $5 million will have to be brought in advance. For equity holding of over 75 percent, $7.5 million will have to be brought in advance and the balance would have to be brought over 24 months. NBFCs wholly owned by foreign equity will be allowed to act only as holding companies.
The Observer
INDIA'S POSITION WORSE THAN OTHERS WITH SAME RATING:MOODY'S

Moody's Investors Service has said it is not prepared to play "political football" in the current controversy over its outlook report on India. Based on purely quantitative indicators, India's position was worse than other countries with identical investment grade ratings, the lead analyst for India's sovereign rating said. Moody's upgraded India's rating in December 1994. However, in a report published in February, Moody's said an unstable political environment, directionless economic policies and a deterioration in the macro-economic balances led to an unfavourable outlook for the country's BAA3 rating.
RELIANCE COMMISSIONS WORLD'S LARGEST CRACKER PLANT

The world's largest multifeed petrochemical cracker plant was commissioned by Reliance Industries (RIL) at its industrial complex at Hazira in the western state of Gujarat. RIL's investment exceeding 100 billion rupees is the largest investment by the private sector at any single site in any state in the country. The complex would house manufacturing facilities for synthetic fibres, fibre intermediates, polymers and chemicals producing in excess of five million tonnes per annum.
